evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Research on Excavated Texts and Paleography, Du Qingyu
evidence.text: The author reports oracle-bone forms whose middle stroke is shorter than the upper and lower strokes, and argues that the small-seal form inherited bronze forms whose strokes later curved to distinguish the graph from 三. He reviews cloud-vapor pictography and several alternative explanations, finding the visible oracle-bone shape insufficient to settle its original construction. This is one scholarly analysis, not a consensus demonstration.
evidence.title: 杜清雨：甲骨文“气”字構形試析

evidence.source: CASE 報科學, National Taiwan University
evidence.text: The article reviews proposals that oracle-bone 气 in 合12532 and 粹771 refers to cloud/rain, and competing analyses involving a sign for cutting or readings related to 迄/訖. It notes disagreement about the syntax of 合6057 气至 and concludes that no known oracle-bone occurrence securely uses 气 as the noun ‘cloud vapor.’ Thus the oracle-bone referent and earliest sense remain disputed.
evidence.title: 甲骨文的「云」與「气」

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: oracle-bone and bronze uses; form changes
evidence.text: This database follows the traditional account that oracle-bone 气 depicts cloud vapor, but separately reports oracle-bone uses read as ‘ultimately’ and ‘until’; bronze examples are read as 乞 ‘request’ or 訖 ‘end.’ It says later upper and lower strokes curved to distinguish the form from 三. Its cloud-pictograph explanation conflicts with the caution in the Fudan and CASE discussions.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 气

evidence.source: Shuowen.cn, digitized 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry defines 气 as cloud vapor and calls it pictographic; Duan Yucai says 气 and 氣 are old/current forms, that 氣 came to be used for cloud vapor, and 餼 was then made for the grain-gift sense. The page lists examples from an oracle-bone specimen labeled 前7.36.2 through early Western Zhou and later bronze, Chu, seal, Qin, Han, and regular-script examples. These are lexicographic claims and a specimen index, not independent proof of the original referent.
evidence.title: 气字说文解字在线查询_气字字形演变_气字说文解字注

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 氣 Shuowen analysis, readings, senses, and citations
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen’s analysis of 氣 as ‘fodder and grain supplied to a guest,’ formed from 米 with 气 as phonetic, and cites 春秋傳 ‘齊人來氣諸侯.’ It distinguishes xì, ‘grain provisions given to a guest,’ from qì senses. For qì it cites Zhuangzi 雲氣不待族而雨 for cloud vapor and Zuǒzhuàn 昭公元年 天有六氣 for atmospheric conditions. The citations establish the dictionary’s cited textual examples, not the dates of the underlying textual layers or a precise semantic chronology.
evidence.title: A02115 氣 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: 詞典網, digitized 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The page reproduces Shuowen’s phonosemantic analysis of 氣: 米 supplies the semantic association and 气 the sound; the cited Spring and Autumn passage uses 氣 for provisions to rulers. Duan Yucai says the later common graph 餼 represents the food-gift word while 氣 was borrowed for cloud vapor. This is a traditional dictionary account; it does not date the graph’s creation.
evidence.title: 氣说文解字原文 - 说文解字 - 词典网

search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected Fudan, CASE, Shuowen.cn, CUHK, and Sinica character-database pages. They reveal a material disagreement about oracle-bone form and referent; several other search results were not used as evidence.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw 气 字形演變 甲骨; 气 file Wikimedia Commons ancient Chinese character 氣 oracle bone; 氣 early bronze inscriptions character gift grain 饋客芻米 金文
search_audit.outcome: Inspected exact Commons descriptions and official Taiwan MOE and dictionary pages. Commons pages supply actual original SVG links and rights statements; the inspected glyphs are digital redrawings. The Xiaoxuetang hit was a usage guide, not a character-specific record.

gaps: The exact ancient referent and initial semantic value of oracle-bone 气 remain unsettled: traditional cloud-vapor pictography conflicts with specialist proposals involving cut/sever, 迄/訖, or other analyses. The available evidence does not establish that the oracle-bone form depicts vapor.

The sources report textual examples but do not establish the dates of their textual layers or the earliest securely dated attestation for cloud vapor, breath, or the atmospheric ‘six qi’ sense. Do not derive chronology from dictionary gloss order.

Shuowen’s grain-provision analysis of 氣 and 气 phonetic role supports the traditional component analysis. The later use of 氣 for vapor and the relation to 餼 are traditional lexicographic accounts; their dates and semantic sequence are not independently resolved here.
No independent evidence was inspected establishing an original object name or pronunciation for the oracle-bone form; no sound-loan argument requiring such an object name is asserted.

The supplied local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were not queried by this web search. Accordingly no official Unihan character-specific record is newly verified, and this response makes no new reading or reconstruction claim.
